subject: PayGrid - Subprocessor addendum: tenant segmentation & legacy service question
messages:
From: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@paygrid.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: procurements@paygrid.com, security@paygrid.com
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2026 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Subprocessor addendum: tenant segmentation & legacy route question

Hi Naomi,

We recently received an update from our legal team asking for a narrow subprocessor addendum that clarifies cross-tenant segmentation guarantees and confirms whether any legacy logging services route tenant-specific payloads to third-party storage. In the proposed addendum attached we've suggested explicit language around:

- Tenant logical separation and access controls
- Data-at-rest and transit protections for tenant logs
- List of subprocessors with roles and countries
- Export controls and CCPA transfer notes

Could you please confirm whether Redwood can sign the attached addendum as-is or if you need alternative language? Specifically, we need to know if any historical / legacy services (we've flagged LogRelay) send unredacted tenant identifiers to a third-party vendor called EdgeStore.

Attachments: [Attachment: proposed_addendum_paygrid_v1.pdf (PDF)]

We're on a tight procurement timeline and have a planned contract signature next week, so any evidence you can share (subprocessor roster, dataflow diagram, SOC 2 attestation) would be appreciated.

Thanks,
Oliver
Director, Security & Compliance
PayGrid
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Subprocessor addendum: tenant segmentation & legacy route question

Karthik / Mina — forwarding PayGrid's request. They want confirmation on tenant segmentation guarantees and whether LogRelay (legacy) sends tenant identifiers to EdgeStore. They attached a proposed addendum; procurement wants a sign-off and security wants evidence. Can you validate the dataflow and what we can provide this week?

Action items: 
- Karthik: quick technical note summarizing current routing for logs and whether any identifiers are stored outside Redwood-controlled buckets (and the retention policy). If LogRelay still touches anything, enumerate which tenants (should be none, but call out any migration windows).
- Mina: attach latest SOC 2 Type II and our subprocessor roster. If we can provide explicit export / CCPA language for the addendum, draft a couple of sentences for legal to review.

I will follow up to consolidate a response to PayGrid; they have a signing sprint next week.

Thanks — Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Manager, Enterprise Security Outreach
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2026 15:26:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Subprocessor addendum: tenant segmentation & legacy route question

Naomi — quick technical summary below; happy to paste this to PayGrid or tighten the language if you want.

Summary:
- Tenant isolation: All active production inference requests are processed in tenant-scoped runtime instances. Models execute in isolated multi-tenant namespaces with per-tenant encryption keys (KMS-backed). No production request payloads or inference outputs are shared across tenant namespaces.
- Logging/observability: Current pipeline splits logs into three tiers: (1) metrics/aggregates (Prometheus) which are tenant-agnostic; (2) structured request traces where we hash tenant IDs for indexing; (3) verbose debug logs (only enabled for specific support windows) which may contain tenant identifiers.
- Legacy service (LogRelay): LogRelay was deprecated in Q1 2026 and was replaced by LogStream. During the migration we had a brief overlap window (Feb 10–Feb 24, 2026) where LogRelay forwarded some debug payloads to EdgeStore for retention. Those payloads were rotated and purged as part of the migration playbook; there are no active flows from LogRelay to EdgeStore now.
- Current third parties: EdgeStore remains in our historical roster as a retired storage vendor (used for legacy debug retention). Active storage and retention are handled by Redwood-controlled buckets in AWS us-west-2 with server-side encryption and access limited to a small SRE group.
- Retention/exports: Any retained debug artifacts from the legacy overlap were purged on 2026-03-01; we can provide the purge job logs if PayGrid needs evidence.

Suggested language for addendum: 
"Redwood certifies that production inference requests and tenant-specific data are processed in logically segregated namespaces with tenant-scoped encryption. No current production routes transfer tenant-identifying payloads to third-party storage providers for read/write access. Historical debug artifacts forwarded to third-party storage during a migration window were purged and are no longer retained."

Attachments I can supply: network dataflow diagram and purge job logs. Let me know if you want me to redact anything before sharing.

- Karthik
Lead Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 31 Aug 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Subprocessor addendum: tenant segmentation & legacy route question

Adding SOC2 and roster materials.

I've attached the following: 
- SOC2-Type2-2026.pdf (redacted to remove customer-specific examples)
- subprocessor_roster_v4.xlsx (current active + retired markers; columns: name, role, country, active_bool, last_poc)
- dataflow-diagram.svg (simplified view of tenant routing)

Notes: 
- EdgeStore is marked as retired (retirement_date: 2026-03-01).
- Purge evidence: we have the purge job ID PJ-20260301-88 and logs; if PayGrid requires, legal can provide the log export under an MSA non-prod evidence share.
- Proposed phrasing for export/CCPA: "Redwood does not transfer customer personal data to subprocessors outside of the locations listed in the subprocessor roster; retired processors with historical retention have documented purge dates and attestations available upon request."

Attaching files now. I can coordinate with Legal to sign the addendum once Karthik confirms the final phrasing and we decide whether to include retirement/purge sentences.

Regards,
Mina
Head, Compliance Operations
[Attachment: SOC2-Type2-2026.pdf (PDF)]

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@paygrid.com>
Cc: procurements@paygrid.com, security@paygrid.com, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 31 Aug 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Subprocessor addendum: tenant segmentation & legacy route question

Oliver — thanks for the addendum and the heads-up on the signing timeline. Below is a consolidated response and the materials PayGrid requested.

Short answer: We can sign a narrow addendum with the suggested tenant-segmentation language and an explicit retired-processor disclosure. We cannot agree to broad indemnities or open-ended export commitments; our proposed amendments are limited to factual attestations and retention/purge evidence.

What we're providing now (attachments & links):
- Current subprocessor roster (see attached xlsx) — includes active vs retired flags and countries.
- SOC 2 Type II report (redacted) — attached.
- Dataflow diagram (link & attached svg) — shows active routing and the retired LogRelay->EdgeStore path with purge date.
- Purge job reference: PJ-20260301-88. We can export the purge job logs under an evidence share after an NDA/limited access agreement if required.

Suggested addendum clause (legal-friendly):
"Redwood certifies that production request and tenant data are processed in logically segregated namespaces with tenant-scoped encryption. Any historical forwarding of debug artifacts to third-party storage during migration windows has been retired and purged as documented in the subprocessor roster; purge evidence may be provided under a mutually agreed evidence share."

If that language is acceptable, I will route to Legal to execute the addendum. If PayGrid needs the purge logs directly attached, please let us know and we will process an evidence-share request with SRE and Legal.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Manager, Enterprise Security Outreach
Redwood Inference
[Attachments included: subprocessor_roster_v4.xlsx, SOC2-Type2-2026.pdf, dataflow-diagram.svg]
